newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech central bank intervenes to boost crown.
newsitem.headline: Czech central bank intervenes to boost crown.

text.p: The Czech central bank (CNB) intervened on Friday for the second consecutive day to try to shore up the ailing crown and comments by the bank's governor defending exchange rate policy failed to stop the slide.
CNB Governor Jan Vit told Reuters the central bank would stick to its current exchange rate policy and that the exchange rate was manageable within the current +/-7.5 percent fluctuation band.

But Vit's comments failed to change the bearish market sentiment currently running roughshod over the crown, pushing it to 4.13 percent on the depreciation side of its dollar/mark basket parity and prompting a fresh wave of intervention.
"After the comments everybody from London...provocatively bought currency against the crown, so the crown was weaker than before," said Petr Korous of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka.
"Sentiment is very bearish," he added.
In explaining why the CNB entered the market, Vit said the crown's fall was not due to domestic economic factors but reflected developments on financial markets abroad.
He did not elaborate, but some traders said foreign investors were getting nervous over some emerging market economies troubled by a weak external position, such as Thailand.
"We still think that the proper level of the exchange rate is within the fluctuation band, and we are using our own instruments including intervention to keep it in," Vit added.
It was the second main wave of intervention by the CNB on Friday but dealers said the CNB still faced an uphill battle if it was going to firm up market sentiment.

"The central bank is going to have a tough time keeping the crown up, sentiment is very weak. We may see London and New York wait until central bank activity eases and at about 1300 GMT they may jump on the crown," Korous said.
He added that major players knew the CNB was on the defensive, making the crown vulnerable to further attacks.

After warning the market for months it would not allow the crown to fall too much, the central bank first stepped into the market on Thursday with several rounds of intervention and vowed to continue buying crowns if necessary.

The CNB kept its promise, entering the market at about 0800 GMT by first checking rates and then striking deals at around four percent on the depreciation side of its dollar/mark parity. The bank also raised its one-week repo rate by 50 basis points to 12.90 percent.
Central bank officials confirmed the actions, adding volumes were small. At the end of March, the CNB's foreign exchange reserves were almost unchanged from the month before at $11.7 billion.
The crown opened Friday at about 3.8 percent on the depreciation side of its dollar/mark basket midpoint, but lost ground to around -3.95 percent despite the repo rate rise.
Dealers said they thought the move was far too small to provide any real support for the crown.

"I don't think such a change in rates will effect the market at all. If the central bank is going to protect the crown it has to do something more significant, not just a few basis points," said Breta Tichanek of ING Bank.
Another trader added: "The repo rate rise was already built into the market, so its effect is minimal."
Late on Thursday the CNB said it had decided to raise its repo rate, but had not set a target for how much, instead allowing "market conditions" to be the determining factor.
Tomas Becvar of Komercni Banka said that while the CNB intervened at around five percent on the depreciation side of basket parity on Thursday, its Friday activities began at a higher level.
"They (the CNB) will try to keep it (the crown) under four percent, but so far it's been a fifty-fifty fight," Becvar added.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
